summary: Frontend Live Work testing completed: core start, reverse timer, pause disposition, priority transfer, completion metrics, refresh persistence, disabled unassigned actions, and shell navigation passed. Individual OLI search exposed duplicate seeded IDs.

integration_issues.flow: Individual OLI search and ID-keyed actions
integration_issues.issue: The demo seed contains duplicate OLI ID OLI17495576578710 (first record and final GST record). Searching an individual OLI ID returns 2 rows instead of 1; React rows also share the same key and start/priority state updates compare by id, so actions can affect both records or the wrong record.

action_items: Make all 17 seeded OLI IDs unique, then retest individual search and transfer/start behavior.
critical_code_review_comments: seed assigns the same OLI ID to i=0 and i=16; all state mutations use id equality and table keys use id, making duplicate IDs a correctness issue beyond display.
seed_data_creation: Used existing browser demo seed only; cleared localStorage before the primary flow run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Core Live Work flows passed on clean state. Retest after unique OLI seed IDs are corrected; timer-expiry branches were not waited for because demo timers are 20-30 minutes.
rca of the issue: In App.js seed, i=0 generates OLI17495576578710 while the i=16 special case also hardcodes OLI17495576578710. The UI filters by ID, renders key by ID, and updates items with x.id===item.id, so duplicates are not safely addressable.
